title: Is forty two, a multiple of seven, divisible by twenty eight?
description: Thirty six is divided by every factor of twelve, and one hundred and eight is shown to be divisible by twelve. Then forty two is written as seven times six, and fourteen divides it but twenty eight does not. Keeko raises the doubt that forty two is divisible by seven, so it is divisible by twenty eight.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number divisible by twelve is divisible by every factor of twelve, but a number divisible by seven is divisible by seven times a second number only if that second number divides the rest. Watch for students who think a multiple of seven is divisible by every multiple of seven.

source: 36 is divisible by 12. Check that 36 is divisible by every f
video_script.why: A learner checks that a number divisible by twelve is divisible by each factor of twelve, then tests forty two against fourteen and twenty eight by writing it as seven times six.
video_script.substitution: the book's own numbers: thirty six, twelve, one hundred and eight and forty two
video_script.anchor: dots in groups of twelve split into smaller equal groups
video_script.wrong_answer: forty two is divisible by seven so it is divisible by twenty eight
video_script.wrong_move: thinks that a number divisible by seven is divisible by every multiple of seven, without dividing to see what is left over
video_script.payoff_line: Thirty six passes every factor of twelve, and one hundred and eight is divisible by twelve. Forty two is divisible by fourteen but not by twenty eight.

final_answer.value: 36 passes every factor of 12 and 108 is divisible by 12 (always true); 42 is divisible by 14 but not by 28 (sometimes true)
final_answer.spoken: thirty six passes every factor of twelve, and one hundred and eight is divisible by twelve. Forty two is divisible by fourteen but not by twenty eight

hold_back: 36 passes every factor of 12 and 108 is divisible by 12 (always true); 42 is divisible by 14 but not by 28 (sometimes true)
maths_rules: 42 = 7 x 6; 14 = 7 x 2 and 2 is a factor of 6, so 42 / 14 = 3
28 = 7 x 4 and 4 is not a factor of 6; 42 = 28 + 14, remainder 14
a multiple of 7 is divisible by 7 x k only if k is a factor of the number it is 7 times
video_script.design: One idea: a number divisible by twelve is divisible by every factor of twelve, but being divisible by seven does not give divisibility by every multiple of seven. Assumes factors and division facts. Wrong idea: divisible by seven means divisible by twenty eight. Groups of dots stay on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about factors and multiples.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Thirty six is divisible by twelve. Is it divisible by every factor of twelve? Is one hundred and eight divisible by twelve?
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Forty two is a multiple of seven. Is it divisible by twenty eight and by fourteen?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Twelve dots split into equal groups of one, two, three, four, six or twelve.
<bookmark mark='same'/>A pile made of whole groups of twelve splits the same ways.

beats.on_screen: Given: 36 is divisible by 12; 108 is a multiple of 36; 42 is a multiple of 7
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, thirty six is divisible by twelve. One hundred and eight is a multiple of thirty six, and forty two is a multiple of seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: is 36 divisible by each factor of 12? Is 108 divisible by 12? Is 42 divisible by 28? by 14?
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which of these divisions come out whole.

marks.list: the factors of twelve are listed
marks.small: thirty six divided by one, two and three gives thirty six, eighteen and twelve
marks.big: thirty six divided by four, six and twelve gives nine, six and three

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step one, list the factors of twelve. They are one, two, three, four, six and twelve.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Thirty six divided by one, two and three gives thirty six, eighteen and twelve.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Divided by four, six and twelve it gives nine, six and three. All of them come out whole.

marks.mult: one hundred and eight is written as thirty six times three
marks.twelve: thirty six is written as twelve times three, and the groups of twelve are counted as nine

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step two, look at a multiple of thirty six. One hundred and eight is thirty six times three.
<bookmark mark='twelve'/>Thirty six is twelve times three, so one hundred and eight is twelve times three times three. That is twelve times nine.

marks.seven: forty two is written as seven times six
marks.fourteen: fourteen is written as seven times two, and two goes into six three times

narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step three, write forty two as seven times six.
<bookmark mark='fourteen'/>Fourteen is seven times two, and two is a factor of six. Fourteen divides forty two exactly, three times.

beats.on_screen: 28 = 7 × 4; 4 is not a factor of 6; 42 = 28 + 14, remainder 14

marks.twentyeight: twenty eight is written as seven times four, and four is not a factor of six
marks.left: twenty eight is taken from forty two and fourteen are left

narration: <bookmark mark='twentyeight'/>Step four, try twenty eight. It is seven times four, and four is not a factor of six.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Take twenty eight from forty two, and fourteen are left. Twenty eight does not divide forty two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 36 passes every factor of 12 and 108 is divisible by 12 (always true); 42 is divisible by 14 but not by 28 (sometimes true)

marks.kinds: the words always true and sometimes true glow in turn

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Thirty six passes every factor of twelve, and one hundred and eight is divisible by twelve. Forty two is divisible by fourteen but not by twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='kinds'/>The claims about thirty six and one hundred and eight are always true. The claim about forty two is sometimes true.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks forty two is divisible by seven so it is divisible by twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='left'/>But take twenty eight from forty two, and fourteen dots are left over.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Twenty eight is a multiple of seven, but it does not go in exactly.
